chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
The dragon did not move.

Neither did I.

That seemed fair for the first few seconds.

Then it became his choice.

I had just told a creature older than my kingdom that the future he remembered me not being part of had happened with me in it once already.

There were several reasonable responses to that.

Disbelief.

Questions.

Eating me.

I had prepared for two of those.

Ithar stared.

I shifted my weight off the bad leg.

The movement was small.

His eye followed it anyway.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
“I remember another life. Approximately forty years. Nineteen to fifty-nine.”

Nothing happened.

I had expected that sentence to feel larger.

It did not.

It sounded exactly like what it was.

A man in a cave saying something impossible.

“The childhood before that was the same. Or close enough that I never found a difference worth keeping. I did not return to birth. I woke at nineteen.”

His eye moved over my face.

Then lower.

The ruined leg.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
The answer came out lighter than the thing underneath it.

At nineteen I had two good knees.

Two good hands.

A shoulder that had not learned weather.

Ithar did not follow me into that.

That was almost kind.

Almost.

The claw nearest the old Line disk moved once through the gold.

Coins made a soft dry sound against one another.

I knew what he wanted next without hearing the question.

What had I been in the first life?

Not Greg.

The other answer.

“Ranker.”

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
The sudden lift beneath my stomach when the thing under the plate swelled.

I had forgotten the sky.

I remembered the smell perfectly.

“There was a membrane underneath. Tough. Thin. I thought it was another layer of armor until it inflated hard enough to throw me off. I cut it. Thought it was a weakness. Never knew what it actually did.”

The dragon went still.

Completely.

That was starting to mean more than movement.

Then Ithar spoke for long enough that I stopped waiting for my turn.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
I rubbed my face.

It had been a long climb.

It was becoming a longer conversation.

“I knew her as Nhal.”

Nothing happened.

Then Ithar's pupil narrowed.

That was enough.

“Ah.”

I did not like the way he said it.

Then, instead of making me drag the questions out of him one at a time, he gave me the problem whole.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
“I do not know whether you moved backward through time. I do not know whether the world repeated. I do not know whether another Greg lived and left something inside you. I do not know whether the distinction between those possibilities is meaningful at the scale involved.

“I know only that your explanation is no longer the least interesting possibility.”

I stared at him.

“Scale involved.”

His eye held mine.

“You think this is bigger than me.”

Ithar's mouth shifted.

Not quite a smile.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
He did not need to say that almost everything was bigger than me.

The thought arrived in his face well enough.

“Fair.”

I looked at the old disk between us.

Then at the wall where his coin was still buried.

Then at the passage out.

My knee hurt.

The Line was failing below the mountain.

Two point three million people were still inconveniently mortal.

And somehow I had lost control of the negotiation badly enough that the dragon was examining my existence instead.

“The Line.”

chunks.title: THE BARGAINER
chunks.transcript: “You came here because of the Line. That is not the same as coming here for the Line. You knew my name before the western stations began failing. You knew the mountain before the ninth station bled pressure into the eastern sink. You knew Nhal had known me before your present kingdom appointed the first keeper now attempting to repair that station. You searched for me before the crisis you offered as your reason for arriving.

chunks.title: THE BARGAINER
chunks.transcript:
That was not finishing by any human definition I respected.

Apparently the dragon had his own.

I laughed once through my nose.

The sound came out meaner than I intended.

“Do you want payment? Gold? Land? You like mountains. I could probably find you another one.”

His mouth shifted.

“I possess enough mountain.”

I looked around.

“Good sentence.”

The mouth moved again.

Not quite a smile.

Neither of us spoke for a moment.

That might have been our first successful exchange.

“I am not telling you eighty years.”

chunks.transcript:
“That sounds suspiciously like rules for my story.”

Ithar's eye held mine.

“Life Two is the spine. Life One where it matters.”

The eye did not move.

“And I get some editorial control.”

A long pause.

Very little, apparently.

“More than none.”

His mouth shifted.

Acceptable.

That was easier than expected.

Which probably meant I had misunderstood the agreement.

Ithar was going to be fucking annoying about this.

At least we were clear.

I thought about time next.

Human time.
